title: Statistical Inference II
description: The Statistics Department's second inference course: sampling and sampling distributions, point estimation and the properties of good estimators, confidence intervals for means, proportions, variances and differences, sample size, the principles of hypothesis testing with Type I and II errors and power, tests on means, proportions and variances, chi-square tests, analysis of variance and simple regression. Built from Dr A. Adedayo Adepoju's STA 221 lectures (2021), the course outline and the past papers from 2009/10 to 2020/21.

topics.title: Sampling and Sampling Distributions
topics.summary: A sample is studied because the whole population usually cannot be. STA 221 covers the sampling methods, sampling and non-sampling error, and the sampling distributions of the mean and of a proportion, with and without replacement.
subtopics: Sampling distribution of the mean and the central limit theorem
Sampling distribution of a proportion and of a difference

topics.title: Point Estimation
topics.summary: Estimation uses a sample value to estimate an unknown parameter. A point estimate is judged by unbiasedness, efficiency (mean squared error), consistency and robustness.
subtopics: Robust estimators and the median absolute deviation

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for Means and Proportions
topics.summary: A confidence interval gives a range that contains the parameter with a chosen confidence level. STA 221 builds intervals for a mean with σ known or unknown and for a proportion.
subtopics: Confidence level and the margin of error
Interval for μ with σ known
How confidence and n affect the width

topics.title: Intervals for Variances and Differences, and Sample Size
topics.summary: Intervals for a variance use the chi-square distribution and for a ratio of variances the F-distribution, both for normal populations. Differences of means and proportions get z or t intervals, and sample size is chosen from the confidence level and the bound on the error.
subtopics: Interval for a ratio of variances (F)
Difference of two means: σ known, pooled and unequal variances

topics.title: Principles of Hypothesis Testing
topics.summary: A hypothesis test decides between a null and an alternative hypothesis using a test statistic and a critical region. STA 221 stresses the two kinds of error, the significance level, and the power of a test.
subtopics: Null and alternative, simple and composite hypotheses
Test statistic, critical region and significance level
Type I and Type II errors
Calculating β for a z test

topics.title: Tests on Means, Proportions and Variances
topics.summary: The past papers test one mean, two means, one or two proportions and one or two variances. The choice of z, t, chi-square or F statistic depends on what is known and on the sample size.
subtopics: One mean: z with σ known, t with σ unknown
Two means: z and the pooled t test

topics.title: Chi-square Tests, ANOVA and Regression
topics.summary: Every STA 221 paper ends with chi-square goodness-of-fit and independence tests and one-way or two-way analysis of variance; earlier papers add regression and correlation. These are the outline's goodness-of-fit and ANOVA weeks.
subtopics: Goodness of fit to binomial and Poisson
